The vulnerable code path is absent from the shipped cyrus-sasl2 artifacts. CVE-2026-132138 is a NULL pointer dereference in the SCRAM server when a client sends channel-binding data although the server has no channel-binding configured. The fix is upstream commit 45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86 (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86), which adds a NULL check on the server channel-binding type before it is dereferenced in plugins/scram.c. That check is present in the cyrus-sasl 2.1.28 source that Debian packages, and the built libscram plugin in the shipped libsasl2-modules package contains its error message. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-132138

The affected name-constraints deinitialization code was introduced in GnuTLS 3.8.13 (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/22cba2f35742cef9137de8f1bcbde6ef15e2e979). This package is built from GnuTLS 3.8.9 sources, which do not contain that code, so the defect is not present. DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is under investigation for this CVE. The CVE describes a critical keyUsage extension that is not rejected when it cannot be processed. No candidate fix was identified in the name-constraint and SAN backport set evaluated for this change, so nothing is backported or verified here. The upstream CVE record does not treat this as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, which this package does not adopt. Revisit when a fix is identified, backported, and tested against this package.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed, and a directoryName constraint rejects any leaf with a non-empty subject DN because DN matching is not implemented. A CA whose permitted directoryName constraint is O=Good rejects a leaf with subject O=Evil, with only the root trusted; the same chain under an unconstrained intermediate is accepted. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed. A CA constraint on an SRVName (otherName OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.7) rejects a leaf that carries an SRVName, and an excluded SRVName constraint rejects the chain even when the leaf carries no SRVName. The same SRVName under an unconstrained CA is accepted. UPN, URI and directoryName constraints are covered by the same tests. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is built with --disable-tls11-support (upstream 4ff381e6, RFC 8996), which disables TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and DTLS 1.0 at configure time. In the built package the protocol list contains only VERS-TLS1.2, VERS-TLS1.3 and VERS-DTLS1.2, and TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 priorities are rejected; a TLS 1.2 handshake and a TLS 1.3 handshake succeed. Verified by package/deb/main/gnutls28/tests (TestLegacyTLSVersionsAreDisabled).

Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690

The vulnerable SRP plugin source is absent from the shipped cyrus-sasl2 artifacts. Debian builds cyrus-sasl2 with SRP disabled (--disable-srp, --disable-srp-setpass), and the built libsasl2-2, libsasl2-modules and libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit packages contain no SRP module and no SRP strings. The SRP plugin was removed upstream in commit fb3724f43dc50247ff2bf02135457d6d77031654 (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/fb3724f43dc50247ff2bf02135457d6d77031654). CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.

statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

statements.status_notes: Uncontrolled recursion in xmlParseSGMLCatalog reachable only when a local user parses an untrusted SGML catalog with the xmlcatalog CLI. Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible (using untrusted SGML catalogs makes no sense). The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the trixie 2.9.14 source without invasive multi-function changes for a negligible CLI-only issue. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-8732
